channel.title: StageGlass Desktop Player
channel.description: Stable-channel updates for StageGlass Desktop Player.

item.title: DesktopPlayer 1.7.1
item.description:
Desktop PropPlayer — 1.7.1

  • Finder folders opened early by an actor now preserve the existing Finder and honor their authored Open in New Window behavior without skipping beats.
  • Opening another QuickTime movie always applies that movie's authored window size and brings it forward, preventing surveillance footage from inheriting a previous portrait video's small frame.
  • Scripted QuickTime windows can keep the red close control inert until an authored playback mark is reached. Scene 103.04 uses this to require the Vigil rewind to 1:45 before closing.
  • QuickTime mark stations now let actor playback and scrubbing remain live while operator Next or replay settles the same beat at its authored paused frame. + and = share the same single-key reveal trigger.
  • Finder supports subtle authored macOS file-tag dots for on-set cues without changing file selection or media identity.

item.title: DesktopPlayer 1.7.0
item.description:
Desktop PropPlayer — 1.7.0

  • GarageBand regions now select, move, and trim as individual clips with exact selection chrome, and deterministic take names replace song-section labels. Space toggles transport, app-content drags no longer move the desktop window, and the flat channel EQ has actor-friendly draggable bands with persistent per-track curves.
  • Golden Gate's Dock now samples the staged wallpaper, desktop items, and windows beneath it. Mac device settings support Show and Auto-hide, with bottom-edge reveal and deterministic reset behavior.
  • Free Roam adds temporary operator controls for an always-visible, automatically hidden, or fully hidden Dock; desktop-file visibility; and launching implemented applications that are not pinned in the Dock. These choices reset when the package is reopened and never alter authored state.
  • Scene 103.04's Finder and QuickTime path is hardened for on-camera use: separate Finder windows, first-click file selection, pre-Play scrubbing, forward and backward stop marks, backward zoom reset, remote-close parity, and the single-key wrist-anchored digital reveal all follow reusable authored controls.
  • Finder preserves authored folder receipts and deterministic file identities, preventing scene or device refreshes from consuming the movie-open cue or routing the actor into the wrong application.
  • GarageBand, Dock/device behavior, Finder/QuickTime authoring, and Free Roam presentation state remain compatible with older scene packages.

item.title: DesktopPlayer 1.6.5
item.description:
Desktop PropPlayer — 1.6.5

  • Single-key "enhance" for on-camera video. Scenes can now author stepped zoom jumps that an actor fires with a single bare key press — each press lands an authored magnification and can cut between production takes with the authored pixelate resolve. Shift/Caps Lock/keypad variants all count; operator ⌘+/⌘− steps remain available as a rescue.
  • Authored hotkey triggers now work on desktop. Any beat can carry a custom key trigger (already authorable in PropMaster); the desktop player now serves them with the same debounce and matching rules as the phone.
  • Play-to-mark walls hold in BOTH directions. Fast-forwarding stops at the next authored mark and rewinding stops at the previous one, so free-transport rehearsals can't overshoot a framed moment.
  • Closing a video window as the actor completes its whole chapter. The next authored file click is live immediately — no more dead first click after an actor-owned close, regardless of how the transport got there.
  • Windows from a previous scene can no longer reappear. Stepping backward after switching scenes no longer resurrects a closed window from the scene you left.
  • Zoom + pan polish. Two-finger pan works across zoomed video at every step, pan can never accidentally change the zoom step, and key shortcuts reach the video window even while the on-set never-beep guard is active.
  • Stage Full Screen stability. Fixed a crash when leaving Stage Full Screen and a partial-screen render after display changes.

item.title: DesktopPlayer 1.6.4
item.description:
Desktop PropPlayer — 1.6.4

  • Notification hover works every time. Mousing over a notification now shows the close and Options controls no matter how the notification arrived — stepping forward through a scene no longer leaves banners hover-dead.
  • Banners match real macOS on hover. The card no longer grows when you mouse over it: the close button floats over the corner and the Options pill appears in place, frosting the text behind it the way real macOS does.
  • Stepping backward doesn't replay animations. Notifications already on screen stay put during back-steps instead of re-sliding in on every step.

Desktop PropPlayer — 1.6.3

  • Actor typing works again. Typing on the keyboard during a typing beat (Safari search, desktop search, text editors) now reveals the authored text. A keyboard-quieting guard added in 1.5.2 was silently eating every typing keystroke; stray key presses outside a typing beat are still silenced, so nothing beeps on set.
  • Preview windows can hide their sidebar. Scenes that author a Preview window without the sidebar now open it that way.
  • Zoomed Preview documents no longer trap the mouse. After zooming in on a document, you can again click and drag the other prop windows around the desktop.

Desktop PropPlayer — 1.6.2

  • Live video receive is back. The desktop prop can receive a live video feed over the network again, for shows that need a real live call/feed on the machine.
  • Notification banners behave like real macOS. Hovering over a notification now shows the right close and options controls in the right places, instead of the wrong buttons popping up.
  • Preview documents fill the window. Opening a document in Preview no longer floats a small page in the middle of a big window — it fills the window the way real Preview does.
  • Finder sidebar labels display cleanly. Long labels in a narrow Finder sidebar now truncate with "..." instead of wrapping badly mid-word.

item.title: DesktopPlayer 1.6.1
item.description:
Desktop PropPlayer — 1.6.1

  • GarageBand is playable — record, menus, and transport all work.
  • ENHANCE zoom on video — plus pinch-to-zoom on paused clips.
  • Custom desktop themes do much more — new beats, real phone apps, real Finder icons.
  • Windows behave — smooth drag and resize, reversible close, minimize keeps things running.
  • Notifications behave like macOS — including auto-dismiss and custom icons.
  • Lots of on-camera fidelity fixes — Mail, typing, and more.

item.title: DesktopPlayer 1.5.2
item.description:
Desktop PropPlayer — 1.5.2

Bug-fix release. Both fixes came off a live test of the Melanie MacBook scene.

  • A reset leaves the prop live — after Shift-Escape (or a reset from PropMaster) the actor's first click fires immediately. A scene that opens by re-stating its own Desktop-at-Start arrangement (an "open Finder" beat for a Finder window that is already on screen) no longer parks the prop one beat short of the actor's cue.
  • Spreadsheets look like spreadsheets — .xlsx, .xls, .csv and .numbers files in a Finder window draw a real spreadsheet document icon instead of a blank page.

item.title: DesktopPlayer 1.5.1
item.description:
Desktop PropPlayer — 1.5.1

Bug-fix release.

  • A receiving banner with real progress — you can see a scene arriving, verifying, and loading; failures say so instead of leaving the old scene up silently.
  • Clicks always find their cue — after Shift-Escape or any reset, clicking the authored file/app/cue works even when a wait beat sits in front of it; local reset and remote reset are now the same operation.
  • Smooth scrolling on big image props — a hidden alpha channel in exported artwork was forcing the whole screen through the slow compositing path; images are now flattened at load, so long scrolls glide.

item.title: DesktopPlayer 1.5.0
item.description:
Desktop PropPlayer

  • QuickTime plays authored audio for real — moving playhead, pause resumes at the live position, spacebar play/pause, and Free playback control beats hand the transport to the actor.
  • The Finder window is accurately designed and dynamically scalable.
  • Dock launches bounce like macOS.
  • Scripted scenes protect their windows — destructive chrome is inert for the actor (including Mission Control's hover-close); free roam is fully live.
  • Scenes play back the dressing they inherited from the scenes before them.
  • Local display controls without the operator — brightness up/down on the player itself, color grading on the arrow keys with ⌘/⌥/⌃, a pull-up controls window, and blackout. Shift-Escape now works in windowed mode too.
  • The remote reaches the whole screen — taps/clicks land anywhere, scrolling drives prop surfaces.
  • Mac message notifications match macOS 26.
  • Real glass on Notification Center, Spotlight, and banners.
  • Maps draws the authored route.
  • Messages matches the iPhone — same transcript, deterministic authored times.

item.title: DesktopPlayer 1.4.1
item.description:
Desktop PropPlayer

  • Voice Memos records for real — authored recording lists, live-mic or authored waveforms, and a playable temporary take that reset cleans up.
  • Show-owned Studio skins play back with their art — resolved through export, import, and loading; skin re-import is transactional (a bad file can't erase a working skin).
  • Per-desk login images — one device can have its own login background without touching the shared skin.
  • Solitaire looks like a card game, not glass UI — printed-card backs, compact foundation markers, authorable card-stock colors and boards.
  • Responsive authored office surfaces — Mail, spreadsheets, documents, and login resolve show-owned art and recompose to the window.

item.title: DesktopPlayer 1.3.0
item.description:
Desktop PropPlayer — 1.3.0

  • Stage Full Screen fits the real display. Wide, 16:9, and notched Macs fill every edge without stretching authored windows or leaving black bars.
  • Safari props look and scroll correctly. Tall page artwork starts at the true top, reaches the bottom without snapping back, and overscroll reveals a page-colored canvas.
  • Mac chrome follows the wallpaper. The Dock uses the selected wallpaper instead of a blue reconstruction, and menu text adapts to bright and dark backgrounds.
  • New original wallpapers. Four clearance-safe wallpapers each for Mac, Windows, and Linux.
  • Show-specific desktop apps. A show can place its own interactive app in the Dock, launch it in free roam or from a beat, and keep its data through package loading.
  • Better fleet identification. Persistent seat names, on-screen Identify labels, and role reporting make large desktop fleets easier to manage from PropMaster.
  • Open scenes directly in Free Roam with File > Open Scene.
  • Photos is faster and reads like the real app — smooth scrolling on big libraries, the real dark-scrim header, native notification banners.
  • The remote now fully drives desktop players accurately: blackout toggle, battery level, stage dim, and brightness/grading affect the whole screen including mouse.
  • CMD+OPTION+CONTROL+F for fullscreen. +Q for quit. Dimming will only show in fullscreen so you can otherwise operate the computer normally.
  • Free Roam menu (synthetic filling of data, Dark Mode, Hide Dates) and free-roam Notes typing.
  • Cmd+Q protected during shows; authored status items display (and fit notched Macs).
  • Fixes: launch crash, grading lag, window geometry on back-navigation.

item.title: DesktopPlayer 1.2.0
item.description:
StageGlass Desktop Player — 1.2.0

This update turns PropPlayer into a more dependable on-set Mac prop, with one predictable full-screen mode, explicit startup behavior, stronger scene loading, and a major fidelity pass across the simulated desktop.

  • One Stage Full Screen. The green window button, View menu, and keyboard shortcut now enter the same edge-to-edge stage mode. The menu bar and Dock stay hidden, and the same command always exits cleanly.
  • Choose what opens at launch. Startup settings now offer Reopen Last Session, Open Empty Desktop, and Always Open This Package. Reopen Last is the default and remembers successful local and PropMaster loads of both scene and free-roam packages.
  • Safer package recovery. Startup packages are stored transactionally. A damaged or failed replacement cannot erase the last known-good session, and launch failures now produce a clear error instead of silently opening an unrelated package.
  • Desktop-at-start scenes. Scenes can open with several authored, arranged windows already on screen. Window-targeted beats keep addressing the intended window throughout playback, including multiple independent Safari windows.
  • Better browser props. Safari pages support tall scrolling artwork, reliable page-relative tap zones, typing regions, independent window state, and settled background dressing windows.
  • A camera-ready Mac desktop. Photos gained its production library layout, translucent toolbar, real import flow, sidebar depth, and scene-clock behavior. The Dock, menu bar, wallpaper, sidebars, notifications, and Golden Gate glass now respond to the actual backdrop instead of reading as flat overlays.
  • Custom surfaces and VFX. App Builder surfaces now play natively on desktop with ordered interactions and deterministic replay. Desktop VFX controls add calibrated plate colors, markers, and persistent operator settings.
  • More reliable show control. PropMaster package pushes load and open consistently, disconnected remote sessions release stuck input locks, remote-port recovery is bounded, and free-roam packages load faster with stronger cache validation.

item.title: DesktopPlayer 1.1.1
item.description:
StageGlass Desktop Player — 1.1.1

On-set fixes for the free-roam desktop, driven by law-office set testing.

  • Screensavers are operator-controlled. The idle countdown that could auto-start a screensaver mid-take is gone. Screensavers engage only from the Director remote, and dismiss only on a deliberate click or key press — brushing or moving the mouse no longer kills them.
  • Screensavers and wallpapers are truly full screen. Images now pin to the real window edges at any window size, including under the title bar. The gap that let the bottom of the taskbar peek out beneath a screensaver is closed.
  • Color temperature behaves like camera white balance. Warm and cool adjustments now shift the white point instead of adding colored light, so warm no longer brightens brown set dressing. Wallpaper and screensaver art stretch-renders without cropping or drifting off-center.

item.title: DesktopPlayer 1.1.0
item.description:
StageGlass Desktop Player — 1.1.0

The free-roam desktop grows up: production-art office packs, a living app suite, and a fleet remote.

  • Production-art free-roam packs. Desktops built from licensed production art with measured icon grids, taskbar hotspots, and chromeless art windows that stay pixel-aligned at any window size.
  • A real app suite for background actors. Browser with live history, search and rich authored web pages; Mail; Files with PDF viewing; Word-style documents with full-page scrolling; Firm Chat messenger with typed replies; Calendar; Contacts; Reminders; Notes; Settings.
  • Windows behave like windows. Resize with limits, minimize that animates into the taskbar, up to three windows per app, and per-seat startup layouts so a wall of machines never boots identical.
  • Desktop Wall fleet control (player side). Shuffle to a seeded state, capture and restore exact desktop states between takes, receive pushed packages over the network and auto-open them, and report live thumbnails to the operator.
  • On-set operator controls. Remote screensaver, keyboard/mouse input lock with a local emergency escape, blackout, brightness, and color grading including temperature.
  • Fill Entire Screen mode. Optional fullscreen that extends behind the MacBook camera housing so props read truly edge-to-edge on camera.
  • Quality of life. Ambient idle activity defers to real users, a visible warning when the remote port is taken by another app, and package swaps always start from a clean desktop.

item.title: DesktopPlayer 1.0.0
item.description:
StageGlass Desktop Player — 1.0.0

First signed, notarized, Sparkle-updating DesktopPlayer release.

  • Desktop prop playback in one app. Mac, Windows, Linux, and custom desktop skins ship from the unified DesktopPlayer target for laptop and monitor props.
  • Free-roam desktop foundation. The app includes the free-roam desktop pack runtime foundation for live background desktops and on-rails office screens.
  • NDI-ready macOS distribution. Bundles the DesktopPlayer NDI runtime dependency and ships as a Developer ID notarized DMG.
  • Sparkle updates. DesktopPlayer now has its own stable appcast and Check for Updates... command, separate from StageGlass Director.
